title: Reverse Words in a String II
summary: Given a character array s, reverse the sequence of words within it.
statement: Given a character array s, reverse the sequence of words within it. Words are separated by a single space. Implement the reversal in-place without using additional memory.
constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100,000; each element is one English letter, digit, or ASCII space.
At least one word; no leading/trailing spaces; exactly one space between words.
Modify the original character array without extra array storage. The judge checks s after the call; a returned copy does not count.
hints: Reversing the entire character array also reverses each word’s letters.
After one full reversal, reverse each individual word to restore its spelling.
Swap s[l] with s[r] while l < r. Apply to the whole array, then to each range between spaces, including the final word.
Each character participates in at most two reversals. Index swaps use O(1) auxiliary space and preserve the original array.
editorial: Reverse the whole array using two pointers. Scan for spaces and reverse every word-sized range; treat the end of the array as a final boundary. The first reversal changes word order, and the second restores letters within words. Exactly one space separates words, so no whitespace normalization is needed. Unlike the string-returning Reverse Words exercise, this callable mutates the original character array and returns None.

tests.explanation: The words become “blue is sky the”; letters within each word remain in their original order.
The same character array must become “cats 2 Hi”; uppercase H and the digit 2 are preserved.
